claims.text: Cold rolling followed by recrystallization annealing will refine the grain structure of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The thermomechanical treatment will improve the tensile ductility and uniform elongation of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The thermomechanical treatment will preserve the high strength of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The thermomechanical treatment will preserve impact-triggered energy release.
Conventionally processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a relatively coarse grain structure.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported yield strength of 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported terminal tensile strain of 13.5%.
Room-temperature cold rolling followed by controlled annealing will produce a fine, homogeneous, recrystallized microstructure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Grain refinement increases grain-boundary density.
Grain refinement reduces stress concentrations and delays crack nucleation in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Reduced stress concentrations and delayed crack nucleation permit more uniform tensile plastic deformation.
Fine-grain strengthening can help retain high yield strength.
Fine-grain strengthening can help retain high compressive strength.
The treatment could increase uniform elongation from 13.5% to more than 20%.
The treated alloy's yield strength will remain within roughly 10% of 786 MPa.
The proposed improvement is expected at room temperature under quasi-static tensile loading.
The fully recrystallized fine-grained Co33Cr24Ni33V10 alloy CR750 exhibited a yield strength of 1060 MPa and uniform elongation of 24.1%.

In the cited Co33Cr24Ni33V10 alloy, high strength was attributed to its fine-grained structure and solid-solution strengthening, while ductility was attributed primarily to dislocation- and stacking-fault-governed strain hardening.
The behavior of the proposed treatment at high strain rates or elevated temperatures is unverified.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% baseline is described as terminal tensile strain but is subsequently treated as the baseline uniform elongation. Terminal strain and uniform elongation are distinct tensile metrics unless explicitly shown to coincide.
